account: Lacking an urban social registry, Nigeria's National Social Safety Nets Coordinating Office (NASSCO) built the Rapid Response Register for a government-funded COVID-19 cash transfer. Ward-level poverty maps came from machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to satellite imagery with household-survey labels, by Berkeley and Columbia researchers with World Bank economists. The maps selected 1,163 of the poorest urban wards, population over 20 million. Residents self-registered by USSD after SMS blasts (first wave June 2021), then in-person verification. Human Rights Watch records the program began in January 2021. The PNAS authors state disbursement began mid-January 2021 (day not given; first day of month used). World Bank monitoring reports 49,000 beneficiary households of the government's COVID-CT as of 15 October 2021. It reports over 1.75 million registrations by November 2021, against a government target of one million households.

ai_role.statement: Decisive at the geographic stage: the ML poverty map alone chose which 1,163 wards were eligible. Individual inclusion depended on USSD self-registration and in-person verification, not AI. Payment and registration counts come from World Bank operational documents, not from the map developers. The PNAS paper and World Bank blog are co-authored by the developers.

fields.account: Lacking an urban social registry, Nigeria's National Social Safety Nets Coordinating Office (NASSCO) built the Rapid Response Register for a government-funded COVID-19 cash transfer. Ward-level poverty maps came from machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to satellite imagery with household-survey labels, by Berkeley and Columbia researchers with World Bank economists. The maps selected 1,163 of the poorest urban wards, population over 20 million. Residents self-registered by USSD after SMS blasts (first wave June 2021), then in-person verification. Human Rights Watch records the program began in January 2021. The PNAS authors state disbursement began mid-January 2021 (day not given; first day of month used). World Bank monitoring reports 49,000 beneficiary households of the government's COVID-CT as of 15 October 2021. It reports over 1.75 million registrations by November 2021, against a government target of one million households.

fields.account: Lacking an urban social registry, Nigeria's National Social Safety Nets Coordinating Office (NASSCO) built the Rapid Response Register for a government-funded COVID-19 cash transfer. Ward-level poverty maps came from machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to satellite imagery with household-survey labels, by Berkeley and Columbia researchers with World Bank economists. The maps selected 1,163 of the poorest urban wards, population over 20 million. Residents self-registered by USSD after SMS blasts (first wave June 2021), then in-person verification. Human Rights Watch records the program began in January 2021. The PNAS authors state disbursement began mid-January 2021 (day not given; first day of month used). World Bank monitoring reports 49,000 beneficiary households of the government's COVID-CT as of 15 October 2021. It reports over 1.75 million registrations by November 2021, against a government target of one million households.

purpose: Geographically target a COVID-19 urban cash transfer to the poorest wards where no social registry existed.

ratings.reason: Households in selected wards were beneficiaries of the government's COVID-CT. The PNAS authors say disbursement began mid-January 2021. The World Bank ISR records 49,000 beneficiary households as of 15 October 2021 without saying how many had been paid.
NASSCO stood up an urban registry within months through USSD self-registration guided by the ML poverty map. Over 1.75 million registrations succeeded (PAD, Nov 2021).
Material to many: 1,163 wards with over 20 million residents made eligible. PNAS simulation finds the ML maps would cut inclusion errors by 61.7% versus the survey-based benchmark.

summary: ML poverty maps chose 1,163 poorest urban wards for Nigeria's COVID-19 cash register; 49,000 beneficiary households as of 15 October 2021
system: Ward-level poverty maps from supervised machine learning (deep learning) on satellite imagery, used for geographic targeting in the Rapid Response Register
taxonomy_note: The good for households is cash, and the type names the register's reach into urban wards it could not otherwise cover.
title: Nigeria's Rapid Response Register used machine-learning poverty maps to select 1,163 urban wards for COVID-19 cash transfers
